_note: All meditation content lives here so a future native app can reuse it unchanged. dow: 0=Sun..6=Sat. 'say' holds every spoken line for a day; 'common' holds lines shared by all days. Each line becomes one recording (audio/<day>-<key>.mp3 or audio/common-<key>.mp3). breath.pattern: [phase, seconds, cue] where phase is in | out | hold | holdout | pump | free, and cue is a 'say'/'common' key (in and out rotate through in_a..c / out_a..c). breath.lines: [seconds into the step, key] for spoken reminders when there is no pattern.

common.settle: Put the phone down... and settle in. We'll begin in a moment.
common.breath_end: Now let the breath return to its own rhythm.
common.body_1: Bring your attention down to your feet... and the ground beneath you.
common.body_2: Let the legs grow heavy. Let the hips settle.
common.body_3: Soften the belly. Let the chest rise and fall on its own.
common.body_4: Release the shoulders... the arms... all the way to the fingertips.
common.body_5: Soften the face. The jaw. The space between the eyes.
common.ask_after: Let it rest there. You don't need an answer.
common.meditate: Now let go of the technique, and the question. Just sit. When a thought pulls you away, notice it... and come back to the breath.
common.complete: Session complete. Carry the seal with you.
common.test: This is how the voice will sound during your sit.

days.release: Aang surrenders his fears of harm and danger. The ground is still there.

breath.name: Box breath
breath.read: In for 4, hold for 4, out for 4, hold empty for 4, through the nose.

days.pool: Attention at the base of the spine where you meet the cushion. Picture a pool there, clouded with worry about the week. On every exhale, silently say LAM and feel the cloud settle into the earth.
days.ask: What am I afraid will happen this week? What would I do today if I weren't afraid?
days.seal: Name the one thing that must get done today. Feel it resting on solid ground.
days.teach: Monday theme: grounding before ambition. Cue students to feel three points of contact before any effort.

say.arrive: Lengthen the spine, soften the jaw and shoulders, three slow breaths. Find the base of your spine.
say.intro: Box breath. In through the nose for four... hold for four... out for four... and hold, empty, for four. Follow my voice.
say.pool: Now rest your attention at the base of the spine, where you meet the cushion. Picture a pool there, clouded with worry about the week. On every exhale, silently say lam... and feel the cloud settle into the earth.
say.ask: What am I afraid will happen this week? What would I do today... if I weren't afraid?
say.seal: Name the one thing that must get done today. Feel it resting on solid ground.

days.release: Aang forgives himself for running away and for the hurt it caused.

breath.name: Nadi Shodana
breath.read: Alternate nostrils. Start by inhaling left, exhaling right. Then inhale on the side you just exhaled from, and switch. In for 4, out for 6.

days.pool: Attention in the low belly and sacrum. Picture water there, slow and muddy with old regret. With each exhale, silently say VAM and let the water move and clear.
days.ask: What am I still punishing myself for? Can I forgive it today and keep the lesson?
days.seal: Name one thing you will enjoy today without earning it first.
days.teach: Tuesday theme: fluid hips and forgiveness. Pair with Goddess and slow hip circles.

say.arrive: Lengthen the spine, soften the jaw and shoulders, three slow breaths. Find your low belly and sacrum.
say.intro: Nadi Shodana. Alternate nostril breathing. Close the right nostril with your thumb... we'll begin by breathing in through the left.
say.pool: Now rest your attention in the low belly and sacrum. Picture water there, slow and muddy with old regret. With each exhale, silently say vam... and let the water move, and clear.
say.ask: What am I still punishing myself for? Can I forgive it today... and keep the lesson?
say.seal: Name one thing you will enjoy today, without earning it first.

days.release: Aang accepts his role as a firebender despite his past mistakes.

breath.name: Kapalabhati
breath.read: Two rounds of about one minute. Pump: short, sharp belly exhales while the soft ticks play (about 30 seconds). Then a full inhale, hold with the bandhas, release slowly, breathe naturally. Lying down? Slow belly breaths instead.

days.pool: Attention at the stomach, just under the ribs. Picture a fire there, smothered by old embarrassment. With each exhale, silently say RAM and let the flame stand up straight.
days.ask: Where am I holding back because of a past mistake? What would I build if that mistake didn't define me?
days.seal: Choose the hardest task on today's list. Commit to its first step before noon.
days.teach: Wednesday theme: no shortcuts. Core work and holds; cue effort without force.

say.arrive: Lengthen the spine, soften the jaw and shoulders, three slow breaths. Find your stomach, just under the ribs.
say.intro: Kapalabhati. Sharp exhales from the belly, with the ticks. Let each inhale happen on its own. I'll tell you when to hold.
say.pump: Pump... sharp exhales from the belly.
say.pool: Now rest your attention at the stomach, just under the ribs. Picture a fire there, smothered by old embarrassment. With each exhale, silently say ram... and let the flame stand up straight.
say.ask: Where am I holding back because of a past mistake? What would I build... if that mistake didn't define me?
say.seal: Choose the hardest task on today's list. Commit to its first step before noon.

days.release: Love is energy. It stays in the heart and is reborn in new forms.

breath.name: Long, deep breathing
breath.read: Slow Ujjayi through the nose. Fill belly, ribs, then chest for 5. Empty in reverse for 7.

days.pool: Attention in the center of the chest. Picture clear air there, heavy with something you lost. With each exhale, silently say YAM and let the air move freely again.
days.ask: What loss am I still carrying? Where has that love already shown up in a new form?
days.seal: Name one person you will show up for today, and how.
days.teach: Thursday theme: open chest, open heart. Backbends with long exhales.

say.arrive: Lengthen the spine, soften the jaw and shoulders, three slow breaths. Find the center of your chest.
say.intro: Long, deep breathing. Slow Ujjayi through the nose. Fill the belly, the ribs, then the chest... and empty in reverse.
say.pool: Now rest your attention in the center of the chest. Picture clear air there, heavy with something you lost. With each exhale, silently say yam... and let the air move freely again.
say.ask: What loss am I still carrying? Where has that love already shown up... in a new form?
say.seal: Name one person you will show up for today... and how.

days.release: Aang stops lying to himself and accepts who he is.

breath.name: Long exhale
breath.read: In for 4. Out for 8 through a soft Ujjayi, letting a silent HAM ride the whole exhale.

days.pool: Attention at the throat. Picture a narrow stream there, jammed by things left unsaid. With each exhale, silently say HAM and feel the channel widen.
days.ask: Where am I not telling myself the truth, about my work, my ventures, or what I really want?
days.seal: Choose one honest message or conversation you've been delaying, and decide when it happens.
days.teach: Friday theme: Satya. Cue students to notice where they perform a pose versus feel it.

say.arrive: Lengthen the spine, soften the jaw and shoulders, three slow breaths. Find your throat.
say.intro: Long exhale. In for four... and out for eight, through a soft Ujjayi... letting a silent ham ride the whole exhale.
say.pool: Now rest your attention at the throat. Picture a narrow stream there, jammed by things left unsaid. With each exhale, silently say ham... and feel the channel widen.
say.ask: Where am I not telling myself the truth? About my work, my ventures... or what I really want?
say.seal: Choose one honest message or conversation you've been delaying... and decide when it happens.

days.release: All four elements, and all people, are connected as one.

breath.name: Sama Vritti
breath.read: Equal breath: in for 5, out for 5, through the nose. Eyes closed, gaze softly up toward the brow.

days.pool: Attention between the eyebrows. Picture a still pool of light there, fogged by the stories you tell about yourself and others. With each exhale, silently say OM and let the fog lift.
days.ask: Where am I seeing separation that isn't there, between my work, my practice, my ventures, and the people in them?
days.seal: Look at the week ahead. What one thread connects everything you're building?
days.teach: Saturday theme: third eye and balance poses. Drishti as a teaching tool.

say.arrive: Lengthen the spine, soften the jaw and shoulders, three slow breaths. Find the center of your forehead.
say.intro: Sama Vritti. Equal breath... in for five, and out for five, through the nose. Let the closed eyes gaze softly up toward the brow.
say.pool: Now rest your attention between the eyebrows. Picture a still pool of light there, fogged by the stories you tell about yourself and others. With each exhale, silently say om... and let the fog lift.
say.ask: Where am I seeing separation that isn't there? Between my work, my practice, my ventures... and the people in them?
say.seal: Look at the week ahead. What one thread connects everything you're building?

days.release: To open the last pool, Aang has to let go. He chose to hold on. Notice what you choose.

breath.name: Counting breath
breath.read: Natural breath, no control and no tones. Count each exhale from 1 to 10, then start again. Lose count? Back to 1, no judgment.

days.pool: Attention at the crown of the head. Picture an opening there, a stream that rises upward, blocked by everything you're gripping. No sound today. Let each exhale loosen your hold.
days.ask: What am I gripping that I don't require right now? What would it feel like to put it down for a week?
days.seal: Release last week. Name one thing you will not carry into the next one.
days.teach: Sunday theme: Aparigraha. Long Savasana; cue letting the floor take the weight.

say.arrive: Lengthen the spine, soften the jaw and shoulders, three slow breaths. Find the crown of your head.
say.intro: Counting breath. Let the breath be natural... no control. Count each exhale, from one to ten... then begin again.
say.count_lost: If you lose count... simply begin again at one.
say.count_soft: No effort. Just counting each exhale.
say.pool: Now rest your attention at the crown of the head. Picture an opening there, a stream rising upward, blocked by everything you're gripping. No sound today. Just let each exhale loosen your hold.
say.ask: What am I gripping that I don't require right now? What would it feel like... to put it down for a week?
say.seal: Release last week. Name one thing you will not carry into the next one.
